mechanismText.text: The Santa Bárbara mercury deposit at Huancavelica was brought to Spanish attention in 1563 or 1564.
The Spanish crown administered its mercury as a monopoly and distributed it to registered refiners at Potosí.
In the early 1570s those refiners adopted amalgamation.
Amalgamation lost mercury during processing, so refining at Potosí's scale required a continuing supply of replacement mercury
— and the crown's Huancavelica mercury became a major source of that supply for Potosí's refiners.

That is why the relationship is drawn in this direction: Huancavelica's mercury supply helped enable the refining change at Potosí. Historians treat this as the mainstream explanation; the Claims it rests on are listed beneath it, and so is what the opposite direction would actually mean.

participants.text: The Spanish crown — administered the Huancavelica mercury as a monopoly and distributed it to Potosí's registered refiners
Registered refiners at Potosí — received the distributed mercury; adopted amalgamation in the early 1570s
The viceregal administration of Peru — named as the source of "a viceregal mercury supply"

Francisco de Toledo, Viceroy of Peru — named here as the holder of the viceregal office in 1573, in office since 1569. **No Claim in this pilot describes his personal role in the mercury supply or in the adoption, so none is stated.**
Affected: workers at Huancavelica and in the Potosí refineries; Andean communities of the sixteen highland provinces conscripted for Potosí from 1573

connection.evidenceIndependenceNote: 3 Sources cited in support. None is a primary record; all three are later scholarship descending from lineages L1, L3 and L5 in the lineage table. Three citations are not three confirmations.

reverseDisclosure.body: Potosí → Huancavelica would be a different Connection, not this one read backwards. Whether demand from Potosí's refiners changed what happened at Huancavelica — its output, its labour, its harm — has its own mechanism and would need its own Evidence. That Connection has not been researched in this pilot, so it is not drawn, not classed, and not described here beyond this note.

connection.reverseRelationshipNote: A separate Connection, not an inversion of this one. Potosí → Huancavelica is not created in this fixture, has no id, no relationship type, no mechanism Claims, and no Evidence. If researched, it gets its own record.

To catch spam, it may send your IP address, and your email if you leave one, to the spam filters CleanTalk and Akismet. The editor also sees your IP address, in the email that carries your report. readingPaneEmpty.heading: One moment, and how we know it.
body: Select the Event on the map, or in the list beneath it, to open its Story.

This pilot covers two moments in 1573. This one is the adoption of mercury amalgamation refining at Potosí, around 1572–1575, and the one Connection this pilot explains for it — from the mercury mine at Huancavelica. The other Places on the map are there to locate that Story. No Story has been researched for them yet. The other moment, Manila, is in the list under "Moments in 1573".
